question: A content team wants Claude to draft a press release, have the draft checked against their style guide, and then produce a revised version based on that check, with each stage logged separately for review. How should this drafting workflow be set up?
options: A) Ask Claude to draft the release ten different ways and pick the best one
B) Ask for the draft, the style review, and the revision all together in a single response
C) Chain three calls: draft the release, review it against the style guide, then refine it
D) Skip the review step and have Claude produce only a final polished draft
correct_answers: C) Chain three calls: draft the release, review it against the style guide, then refine it
explanations: Incorrect. Generating many parallel drafts without a review step against the style guide does not fulfill the requirement to check drafts against specific criteria before revising.
Incorrect. Bundling all three stages into one response does not give the team separately logged and inspectable outputs at each stage.
Correct. This is the self-correction chaining pattern for drafting tasks: generate a draft, review it against criteria, then refine, with each step as a separate, inspectable call.
Incorrect. Skipping the style guide review removes the criteria check the team explicitly wants applied before finalizing the draft.
